findings.title: Google token refresh persists the Zod result, not the credential
findings.body: After a Google refresh, the code assigns `key` to the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and writes that object to `credential.key`. That helper returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token. Previously this path saved `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the token itself. The next `GoogleCalendarService` construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and throws, so every successful Google token refresh (credential sync off or on) corrupts the stored credential and breaks Google Calendar until the user reconnects. On the sync path this is worse: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`, which has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws before a valid token can be applied.

findings.title: Salesforce client always crashes: prisma is not imported
findings.body: `getClient` now always exchanges the refresh token and then calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file never imports `prisma`. Constructing `SalesforceCalendarService` (which awaits `getClient`) throws `ReferenceError` before a jsforce connection is returned, so Salesforce event create/update/delete is broken for every install, not only credential-sync installs. Even if prisma were imported, the new access token is saved and then ignored: the connection is still built with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh token) at line 106, and the token request is hardcoded to `https://login.salesforce.com` (line 75), which rejects sandbox and My Domain refresh tokens that must be sent to the org's own token URL. This path also never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the new sync endpoint is not used.

findings.title: Sync token schema requires a literal ZodString property
findings.body: When credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, refresh parsing uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are the strings `"ZodString"` and `"ZodOptional"`, not a catchall for arbitrary fields. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. A normal body such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` therefore fails `safeParse`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` always throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce refresh all go through this helper, so enabling the feature breaks token refresh for those apps instead of accepting an access token plus expiry.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string refresh_token
findings.body: After a successful parse, if `refresh_token` is absent the helper writes the placeholder string `"refresh_token"` onto the parsed object and returns it. Callers persist that object. Office 365 merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential (`refresh_token` is optional on its schema, and Microsoft often omits a new refresh token), so a real refresh token is overwritten with `"refresh_token"` and the next refresh fails permanently. Zoom assigns `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` the same way once the sync schema does not require a refresh token. The placeholder was meant to satisfy schemas, but it is stored as a live secret.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns an unparsed Fetch Response to callers that expect tokens
findings.body: When sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns the raw Fetch `Response` without checking `response.ok` or reading JSON. Callers do not share one return type. Google reads `res.data.access_token` (Gaxios shape). HubSpot treats the result as a HubSpot token (`accessToken`, `expiresIn`) and writes it back as `credential.key`. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` on an axios response. Lark passes the body to `handleLarkError`, which expects a Lark envelope (`code`, `data.refresh_token`, `data.expires_in`). The comment says the endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but none of these callers adapt that shape, so a successful sync response still fails or stores a Response/wrong object. The non-sync branch returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns, so the two branches are not interchangeable.

findings.title: Outbound token sync request is unauthenticated
findings.body: The refresh call that is supposed to retrieve a user's third-party access token sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in a form body. It does not send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, a signature, or any other credential, even though the new inbound webhook authenticates with that secret. Anyone who can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids. The sample client is what self-hosters are told to point at their token endpoint, and nothing in this request tells that endpoint the caller is Cal.com.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as calcomUserId
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with `credentialId` (the credential primary key) as the third argument. That argument is documented and sent as `calcomUserId`. The parent app will look up the wrong user, or no user, and return another user's tokens or an error. The Bigin refresh method never receives `credential.userId`, so this cannot be correct even after the response-shape bug is fixed. When sync is on, the return value is also a Fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `tokenInfo.data` as if it were an axios response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and the refresh throws.

findings.title: Teams refresh replaces the whole credential with the sync body
findings.body: After `refreshOAuthTokens`, the MS Teams adapter JSON-parses the response and saves that object as the entire `credential.key`. The sync contract is only an access token and expiry, so this drops `refresh_token`, `email`, and `scope` from the stored credential. Expiry is computed as `Date.now() + (expires_in || 0) * 1000`; if the sync payload uses a different expiry field, `expiry_date` becomes now and every subsequent call treats the token as expired and refreshes again, rewriting the key each time. With sync disabled the Microsoft token response is a full token object, so this only breaks the new sync path, but that path is what this PR adds.

findings.title: Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
findings.body: The Zoom refresh calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with app slug `"zoomvideo"`. The installed app id written by the Zoom OAuth callback is `"zoom"` (`appId: "zoom"`), and every other integration in this PR passes its real app slug (`google-calendar`, `msteams`, `office365-calendar`, `hubspot`). The parent store will not find a Zoom credential for `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync returns the wrong app or nothing while other apps sync.

findings.title: Webex sync refresh still requires a full Webex token body
findings.body: Webex was switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the body with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `token_type: "Bearer"`, an exact scope literal, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. It does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. A sync endpoint that returns only an access token and expiry, as `refreshOAuthTokens` documents, fails this schema and the refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex credential sync cannot succeed.

findings.title: Credential webhook leaves invalid rows invalid and can duplicate credentials
findings.body: The update path writes only `key`. Credentials previously marked `invalid: true` by a failed refresh stay invalid, so a successful sync from the parent app does not restore the integration. The lookup is also a non-transactional `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` followed by create (lines 62-90). There is no unique constraint handling, so concurrent webhook deliveries (retries) can insert a second credential for the same user and app. Calendar code uses `findFirst`, so later refreshes update an arbitrary row and the other keeps stale tokens. `zod` parse, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` are also uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx.
